title: A/R Summary puts invoices in buckets at 0, 30, 60 and 90 days past due
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in to ShopView as an Admin user.
  • Customer X has exactly one open invoice, due on day D (a day at least 92 days ago), for $10.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Reports menu.
  2. Click "A/R Aging Summary" in the left list.
  3. Set the date chip to day D.
  4. Read customer X's row.
  5. Set the date chip to D + 30.
  6. Read customer X's row.
  7. Set the date chip to D + 31.
  8. Read customer X's row.
  9. Set the date chip to D + 60.
  10. Read customer X's row.
  11. Set the date chip to D + 61.
  12. Read customer X's row.
  13. Set the date chip to D + 90.
  14. Read customer X's row.
  15. Set the date chip to D + 91.
  16. Read customer X's row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 4:

  • $10.00 under Current.

Step 6:

  • under 1-30 Days.

Step 8:

  • under 31-60 Days.

Step 10:

  • under 31-60 Days.

Step 12:

  • under 61-90 Days.

Step 14:

  • under 61-90 Days.

Step 16:

  • under 91 And Over. Total is $10.00 every time.

Why this matters: Wrong boundaries move money between buckets and break QuickBooks reconciliation.

SOURCE: ShopView/shopview at fc08f23 (production v26.45.3), api/src/Reporting/Dashboard/Application/AccountReceivable/Service/AgingCalculator.php:28-47; api/src/Reporting/Dashboard/Domain/AccountReceivable/Enum/AgingBucketEnum.php:15-24; api/src/Reporting/Dashboard/Infrastructure/Doctrine/AccountPayable/Service/DbalApAgingSummaryFetcher.php:91-95; api/src/Reporting/Dashboard/Application/AccountReceivable/Service/AgingCalculator.php:35-36. V1 code, quoted: `if ($daysPastDue <= 0) addCurrent; elseif (<= 30) add1to30; elseif (<= 60) add31to60; elseif (<= 90) add61to90; else add91Plus`

This is the expected behaviour as per the V1 code baseline AR-AP-V1-BASELINE.md (INV-030, INV-031) for epic SV-11315; the A/R and A/P Report Sorting PRD v12 (Confluence 947650561) does not change it. Last checked against build v26.45.4-b8c04e2 (staging) on 11/12/2026.
